एर्वारु: एर्वारु(क) (1) [CUCUMIS MELO LINN. VAR. MOMORDICA DUTHIE ET FULLER] (Chopra; HK; KB 2, p. 1142; Watt CP, p. 438-439); see Duthie 1, p. 340-342; = C. MOMORDICA ROXB. (Avk; Chopra; HK; Kav; KB 2, p. 1142; Nadk. 1, nr. 729); (2) [C. MELO LINN. VAR. UTILISSIMUS DUTHIE ET FULLER] (KB 2, p. 1143); see Duthie 1, p. 340-342; = C. UTILISSIMUS ROXB. (Avk; Bpn, p. 671; Gul; HB; HSu; KB 2, p. 1143; MW; PW; Vśs).
एलवालु: एलवालु (क) Much confusion exists concerning this substance as will become apparent from the material collected: (1) Bpn, कर्पूरादिवर्ग 120: it is also called कपित्थत्वच् (the bark of कपित्थ). Acc. to the Hindī comm. (p. 262-263) the substance is described somewhere in Bhā. pra. as resembling कङ्कोल and smelling like कुष्ठ। In the same comm. three different identifications are made mention of: a) PRUNUS CERASUS LINN., b) GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN., c) MUKIA SCABRELLA ARN. (Index Kewensis: MELOTHRIA MADERASPATANA COGN. = MUKIA SCABRELLA ARN. = MUKIA MADERA-SPATANA M. ROEM). (2) DWH 2, p. 105-107: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN.; p. 105: “This plant is called in Sanskrit वालुक and एलवालुक on account of the number of large raphides contained in the leaves, and which give them the appearance of being full of sand (वालु).” (Raphides are minute intracellular crystals, usually of an acicular form). (3) Gul: cherry tree (PRUNUS CERASUS LINN.). (4) HB, p. 21: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN.; ibid., footnote 70: “एलवालु is mentioned Su. Sū. 38, 14, where Ḍa.'s comm. explains it as a reddish powder (हरिवालुक), resembling that of the seeds of the कृष्णगन्धा (कृष्णगन्धिकफल)। The latter is a name of the horse-radish tree or शिग्रु or शोभाञ्जन;” ibid., p. 91, footnote 74: “In the Phar. Ind. (= DWH) 2, p. 105, it is wrongly identified with वालुक; the seeds, supplied to me by a native druggist, seem to be simply those of chickweed.” (5) HK: quotes the identifications of PW and Hoernle. (6) Kav, p. 37: a kind of red powder made of some seeds obtainable of every native druggist, not identified; p. 294: a fragrant powder of a bark sold under that name; it is believed to come from the Spice Islands; p. 642: Gaṅgādhara takes it as implying तेजवल, a kind of wood apparently dry but juicy within; it is brought from Nepal. (7) KB 2, p. 1187-1188: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN. (8) MW: the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (कपित्थत्वच्); a granular substance (apparently a vegetable of a reddish-brown colour, used as a drug and perfume). (9) PW: the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (कपित्थत्वच्), used medicinally. (10) V 7, p. 67: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES. (11) Vśs: name of a perfume; a red powder sold under that name; the seed of some plant. (12) Ḍa. on Su. Sū. 38, 14 (printed ed., different from Hoernle's text): “a reddish powder (हरिवालुक), resembling the black, fragrant कट्फ-ल;” कट्फल is usually identified as MYRICA NAGI THUNB.
एला: एला Two kinds of एला are distinguished: 1) सूक्ष्मैला or क्षुद्रैला, the small cardamom, and 2) स्थूलैला or बृहदेला, the large cardamom. (1) ELETTARIA CARDAMOMUM MATON (Avk; Bpn, p. 222-223; Cho-pra; Dgv, nr. 308; Dutt; DWH 3, p. 428-436; Gul; HB; HK; IRM 3, p. 149-160; KB 4, p. 2442-2444; Nadk. 1, nr. 924; V 1, p. 147; Vśs; Watt CP, p. 511-517) = E. MAJOR SM. (Avk) = E. REPENS BAILL. (Avk; Nadk. 1, nr. 924) = ALPINIA CARDAMOMUM ROXB. (KB 4, p. 2442-2444); (2) AMOMUM SUBULATUM ROXB. (Bpn, p. 221; Chopra; Dgv, nr. 308; Dutt; DWH 3, p. 436; HK; KB 4, p. 2432-2433; Nadk. 1, nr. 154; V 1, p. 148; Vśs; Watt CP, p. 65); (3) A. AMARUM F. P. SMITH (Nadk. 1, nr. 150); (4) A. XANTHIOIDES WALL. (Dy, p. 788-789); (5) A. KEPULAGA SPRAGUE ET BURKILL (Bpn, p. 224: used as a substitute) = A. CARDAMOMUM ROXB. (NON LINN.) (Roxb., p. 24: एला); (6) A. AROMATICUM ROXB. (Bpn, p. 222: used as a substitute).
एलावालुक: एलावालुक This term occurs Kauṭ. 2, 25, 27 (text p. 79; transl. Kangle p. 178; transl. J. J. Meyer p. 187; transl. Sham. p. 133). Sham. renders it by SOLANUM MELONGENA, without any comment. J. J. Meyer takes it as the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (एलवालुक), but remarks that the reading एलावालुक makes it probable that one should translate: एला and वालुक (i. e. हरिवालुक, the fragrant bark of कपित्थ); Kangle translates: cardamum, वालुक। Acc. to Vśs एलावालुक is a synonym of एलवालुक।
